title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
AI-generated video and image synthesis enabled scammers to create hundreds of fraudulent social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney. The deployment failure happened at the social media platforms themselves, which did not detect or prevent the creation of these fake accounts before they were used to solicit money from vulnerable immigrants. Catching this would have required platforms to verify the identity of account creators, detect synthetic media in uploaded content, or implement review before accounts offering paid legal services could operate.

The scam operated by directing victims to contact numbers on WhatsApp, where criminals sent false contracts and collected payments through consumer payment apps. It is not established whether the AI systems generating the fake media knew they were being used for fraud, or what role the platforms knew they played in hosting the impersonation before removal.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal discovered that scammers created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of him, offering immigration services he never provides. In these fraudulent videos, the fake Leal offers services like US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200 cash. Leal first learned about the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he says the situation has dramatically worsened over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct people to contact a WhatsApp number, where criminals send phony contracts and request payments through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal urges immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and warns against making immediate payments. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams.
